evidence.title: Grafana Alerting Fundamentals — Alert rules
evidence.what_it_decides: An alert rule carries its own evaluation interval; evaluation is engine work preceding notification routing, so evaluate_alert belongs to the alert-rule owner, not the subscription runner.

rationale: Evaluation criteria live inside the alert rule, not subscription delivery; equal identifiers never establish owners, so alert_state becomes canonical owner and subscription_runner imports instead of holding a duplicate.

evidence.title: BigQuery API jobs.query (synchronous query endpoint)
evidence.what_it_decides: Verifies submit-query as a defined wire-level query-service operation, but its reference governs HTTP semantics only; nothing decides placement between result_stream and query_gateway modules.

rationale: External query APIs fix wire behavior, not internal ownership; with no decisive authority and differing margins, non-collapse holds by qualifying local symbol IDs so both definitions stay distinct uncollapsed.

evidence.title: RFC 6749: The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework (Section 3.3)
evidence.what_it_decides: Scopes bind at authorization time by an authorization server; the RFC explicitly leaves implementation placement ungoverned, deciding nothing about policy_projection versus embedded_bridge internally.

rationale: OAuth binds scope at issuance but names no code location for binding operations; repeated identifiers are not owners, so unambiguous qualified identities preserve both distinct bindings without collapse.

evidence.title: HTML Living Standard — Server-sent events
evidence.what_it_decides: Splits stream-resume duty: the stream carries reconnection/lastEventID state while the client EventSource tracks it, naming neither internal module owner; standoff between result_stream and dashboard_runtime stands.

rationale: SSE assigns resume duties to both stream and client layers, confirming a genuine standoff; equal identifiers do not make owners, so the family elects one shared definition others import.

evidence.title: Vega-Lite Documentation — Mark
evidence.what_it_decides: Marks are declared in the declarative view specification alongside data and encoding; declaration belongs to the specification layer, not any renderer implementation.

rationale: Grammar-of-graphics practice places mark declaration in the specification IR renderers consume; identical names gain no ownership, so presentation_ir is canonical and renderer_adapter imports rather than duplicating.

evidence.title: Amazon S3 API Reference — GetObject (Range header)
evidence.what_it_decides: Bucket-plus-key namespace addressing with Range byte retrieval defines platform object-storage access semantics, fixing get_object_range inside storage addressing rather than generic object contracting.

rationale: Platform precedent binds namespace-addressed range reads to storage object identity; duplicate identifiers confer no ownership, so storage_identity is canonical owner and object_contract imports the operation.

evidence.title: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters), Alistair Cockburn, HAT TR 2005.02
evidence.what_it_decides: "A port identifies a purposeful conversation" with "multiple adapters" plugging into one port, so record-publication semantics belong to the port, never provider adapters.

evidence.title: Atlassian Statuspage API Reference
evidence.what_it_decides: Statuspage's incident endpoints define a vendor-hosted publication target, demonstrating the adapter is replaceable plumbing that cannot own maintenance-change recording semantics.

rationale: Ports-and-adapters law makes adapters interchangeable plugs while ports carry semantics; since equal identifiers establish nothing, status-publication-port is canonical and the Statuspage adapter imports.

evidence.title: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters), Alistair Cockburn, HAT TR 2005.02
evidence.what_it_decides: One port admits multiple adapters; support-case record semantics therefore sit at the support-case-port regardless of which provider adapter is plugged in.

evidence.title: Zendesk Support API — Tickets
evidence.what_it_decides: Zendesk-defined ticket schema confirms vendor adapters supply their own resource models, qualifying them out of owning shared support-case recording semantics.

rationale: Rival vendor schemas (TM Forum, Zendesk) prove adapters cannot define shared record semantics; equal names never own, so support-case-port is canonical with adapters importing.

evidence.title: Open Container Initiative Runtime Specification
evidence.what_it_decides: OCI standardizes OS-process containers using Linux namespaces and cgroups, defining isolation for container backends only.

evidence.title: WASI — WebAssembly System Interface
evidence.what_it_decides: WASI applications run in capability-based sandboxes without ambient authority, defining a rival isolation model; no single standard owns a generic isolationbackend trait.

rationale: OCI namespaces/cgroups and WASI capability sandboxing are co-equal standards, confirming deadlock between adapters; non-collapse law makes identical definitions imports of one family-shared owner.

evidence.title: Linux kernel Control Group v2 documentation
evidence.what_it_decides: Kernel docs govern memory limits and pressure accounting but say nothing about trait.reserve placement or reservation-ledger semantics, leaving this collision purely internal.

rationale: Two families attach conflicting meanings to reserve with no external decider; collapsing would erase real semantic difference, so qualified local identities keep ledger-style and runtime-style reservations distinct.

evidence.title: Online controlled experiments at large scale (KDD 2013), Kohavi et al.
evidence.what_it_decides: Confirms peer-reviewed experimentation-platform literature exists at scale, yet defines no assumption-binding type or sealer/compiler split, leaving sealer versus compiler undecided externally.

rationale: Experimentation research nowhere fixes where assumptions bind; within one experiment family the two byte-identical copies violate non-collapse, so they become imports of a single family-elected owner.

evidence.title: RFC 8949: Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR)
evidence.what_it_decides: Defines CBOR data-format encoding including deterministic encoding, but contains no codec-execution-receipt concept, governing encoding—not receipt ownership—so candidate choice stays internal.

rationale: Codec standards define encodings, never receipts; cross-family identical copies still cannot each claim ownership under non-collapse, so san_codec_runtime (non-adapter side) is canonical and consumers import.

evidence.title: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters), Alistair Cockburn, HAT TR 2005.02
evidence.what_it_decides: Ports identify purposeful conversations while many adapters plug in; the maintenance-change contract therefore belongs to the status-publication-port, not vendor implementations.

evidence.title: Atlassian Statuspage API Reference
evidence.what_it_decides: Statuspage incident payloads are vendor-owned wire shapes, proving contract types must be port-held so competing providers remain substitutable adapters.

rationale: Vendor payload schemas confirm adapters cannot author shared contracts; equal identifiers imply no ownership, so status-publication-port canonically owns the contract with adapters importing it.

evidence.title: Stripe — Basic usage-based billing / usage records
evidence.what_it_decides: Stripe defines its own usage-record/Billing Meters schema for reporting customer usage, one vendor-specific event model.

evidence.title: OpenMeter (openmeterio/openmeter)
evidence.what_it_decides: OpenMeter ingests CloudEvents-formatted usage events with attribution and aggregation, a different event model; rivalry leaves usage-event contract ownership a vendor standoff.

evidence.title: CloudEvents Specification (CNCF)
evidence.what_it_decides: Provides a vendor-neutral interoperable event envelope in common formats, but intentionally does not standardize domain usage-billing semantics.

rationale: Stripe usage records and OpenMeter CloudEvents ingestion are irreconcilable vendor models; CloudEvents is envelope-only, so non-collapse routes both families' imports through one journal-port contract.

evidence.title: Online controlled experiments at large scale (KDD 2013), Kohavi et al.
evidence.what_it_decides: Live record confirms the venue/authors of large-scale experimentation practice, but no source names analysis editions or a sealer-versus-compiler ownership split.

rationale: No external authority defines editioned analysis artifacts; byte-identical duplicates across experiment-family modules cannot each own, so they become imports of one family-elected definition.

evidence.title: Online controlled experiments at large scale (KDD 2013), Kohavi et al.
evidence.what_it_decides: Verified experimentation-platform anchor documents the field but specifies no exposure-cut type or cut-stopping versus binding-compiler ownership, so placement remains internal.

rationale: Cut-stopping ownership is decided only by internal method-kernel responsibilities; identical copies across two families may not multiply owners, so one canonical exposurecut definition serves all importers.

evidence.title: Online controlled experiments at large scale (KDD 2013), Kohavi et al.
evidence.what_it_decides: Live KDD record evidences experimentation literature generally yet governs nothing about integrity escalation policies or profile-compiler versus evaluator placement.

rationale: Integrity escalation semantics exist only internally and external sources stay silent; within one experiment family the repeated definition collapses into a family owner whose identity other modules import.

evidence.title: IEEE Task Force on Process Mining — Process Mining Manifesto
evidence.what_it_decides: The field-defining manifesto presents process models as the single shared formalism underlying discovery, conformance, and performance techniques, requiring one process-model notion imported by every method kernel.

rationale: Process-mining doctrine grounds discovery, conformance, and performance alike on one process-model formalism; equal identifiers do not elect owners, so the method-kernel family shares one imported definition.

evidence.title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd edition (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos)
evidence.what_it_decides: Covers forecast reconciliation and workflow yet defines no publication-profile-result type, leaving geospatial versus forecast compiler ownership governed only by internal structure.

rationale: Neither forecasting nor geospatial authorities define a publication-profile result; cross-family byte-identical copies must not become rival owners, so one canonical definition persists and compilers import.
